title: title, arc_penguins, arc_gangsters songs were never loudness-normalised: -14.2 / -14.1 / -12.9 LUFS vs -16 for all 88 others; arc_gangsters true peak +0.2 dBFS (clips)
repro: ffmpeg -i audio/music/<f>.ogg -af ebur128=peak=true -f null - over all 91 songs: 88 sit at -16.1..-15.7 LUFS, TP <= -1.1; these three are the oldest imports and are missing from audio/ACE_LOG.json, so `ace_batch --reimport-all` never touched them. The title screen and the arc-pick screen (title.gd:336 'arc_'+_arc) are the first thing a player hears, then the farm drops ~2-3 LU (gangster: 3.1 LU) - an obvious volume dip on the first song change; arc_gangsters can clip on decode.
fix: Re-level the three files through ace_import's loudnorm path (I=-16, TP=-1.5, keep loop seam): rm then write each file (hardlinks), and add them to ACE_LOG.json (kind music, note 'legacy import, relevelled') so --reimport-all covers them in future. Add a check in tools/sfx_audit.py or a new tools/loudness_audit.py (check.sh) that fails when any audio/music/*.ogg is outside -16 +/-1 LUFS or TP > -1.0.

title: Dialogue talk blip steals an SFX voice round-robin even when free voices exist, cutting off jingles (j_heart/j_gift after a gift, quest_done, levelup)
repro: Music.blip() always takes _sfx[_next_voice % 6] without checking .playing. Giving a gift plays j_heart (2.9 s) / j_gift (2.4 s) on the first free voice, then the reaction line's blip lands on whatever voice _next_voice points at; when that is the jingle's voice the jingle stops dead after ~0.1 s. Same for quest_done/levelup/j_page followed by a story line. sfx()'s 'take over the oldest one' fallback also uses _next_voice, not the oldest, so it can kill a long jingle while a 0.1 s click is the real oldest. VERIFIED headless: tools/probe_c6_14_voices.gd (worktree c6_14) plays j_heart on voice 0, one blip with _next_voice=0 -> jingle stopped.
fix: Give blips their own AudioStreamPlayer (like _steps), or pick a free voice first and only steal a voice whose stream is shorter than 0.5 s. In sfx(): track start time per voice and steal the one with the least remaining time, never a j_/levelup/quest_done voice still playing (protected list).

title: No music ducking under jingles: 2.3-3.2 s musical stingers (j_heart, j_skill, j_treasure, j_secret, levelup, quest_done, j_region...) play over the area song at full level, clashing in key and tempo
repro: grep set_duck: only Ambience (night/storm), battle._duck_music and title/epilogue resets call it. 29 sfx("j_...") calls play on the SFX bus while music stays at MUSIC_DB. ACE jingles were rendered in their own key; over farm/town songs the result is two pieces of music at once. The one place that ducks (battle._duck_music) uses set_duck's fixed 2.0 s tween, so the dip arrives after most of the 2.4 s j_battle_won has played.
fix: In Music.sfx(): when the name is a jingle (j_* except j_buy/j_confirm, levelup, quest_done, craft_done) and longer than 0.8 s, apply a separate jingle duck: music down ~10 dB in 0.12 s, hold for stream length, back up over 0.8 s. Keep it independent of the ambience duck (sum two values: _duck_env + _duck_jingle) so Ambience's periodic set_duck doesn't cancel it. Give set_duck an optional time argument and let battle._duck_music use the jingle duck instead.

title: Battle-end music duck is undone within 0.5 s: Ambience re-sends its own duck value every evaluation and overwrites battle._duck_music's -9 dB
repro: battle._duck_music() calls set_duck(was - 9) and starts a 2 s tween. Ambience._process re-evaluates every 0.5 s and _evaluate() ends with mu.set_duck(duck) (0 by day, -4 at night); because -9 != duck it starts a new tween back up. Net effect: the song barely dips (<1 dB over 0.5 s) under j_battle_won/j_campaign_won and the closing lines, and battle's 4 s restore check then never matches. One shared _duck value with two writers. Probe tools/probe_c6_14_voices.gd: set_duck(-9) then the Ambience-style set_duck(0) -> _duck back to 0.0 immediately.
fix: Split the duck into named layers in Music: set_duck_layer("env", db) for Ambience, ("jingle"/"battle", db, attack_s, release_s) for one-shots, and apply MUSIC_DB + sum(layers). Ambience only writes the env layer; battle uses the jingle layer (or the jingle auto-duck from the previous finding).

title: set_duck's tween is not tracked: it keeps running on the outgoing player after a crossfade swap and stretches a fade-in to 2 s (not audible in a headless probe, but fragile)
repro: Probe tools/probe_c6_14_xfade.gd (worktree c6_14): set_duck(-4) then play('town') - _tw_out still wins each frame and stops the old song at -40 dB on time, so no audible cut in this order; afterwards the stray duck tween keeps writing the stopped player's volume_db back to -12 for 2 s. If set_duck lands mid fade-in, it kills _tw_in and the new song takes 2.0 s instead of the asked fade (DangerMusic's 0.6 s cut-in becomes 2 s if Ambience re-ducks in that window).
fix: Store the duck tween (_tw_duck), kill it in _start(), and when a fade-in is running just retarget it (or drive volume per frame as fade_gain + duck layers) so the requested fade time is kept.

title: Phone-speaker check: 33 of 91 songs carry most of their energy below 150-200 Hz and drop 6-10 dB through a phone speaker, so equal -16 LUFS files play very unequal on Tom's phone (gangster arc worst)
repro: For each audio/music/*.ogg: mean level full vs after a 2x 200 Hz high-pass (phone speaker approximation). Median loss 5.3 dB; worst ending_gangster -10.4, hideout -9.9, arc_gangsters -9.2, shop_gang -8.2, boss_gang -7.8, danger -7.6, battle_siege_gang -7.5, mine_deep -7.5, neon -7.2; best lake/boss_penguin -1.8, night/clinic -2.2. Over 6 dB: arc_gangsters arc_penguins battle_gang battle_siege battle_siege_gang boss_coalbrook boss_colossus boss_gang boss_light_eater bowling_alley campaign_map colony_ember colony_kelp combat_light_gang countryside danger docks ending_gangster hideout keeper marked mega_desert_temple mine mine_deep moon neon quarry raid rec_center shop_gang sky underground uptown. On the phone, walking farm(penguin, light) -> hideout sounds like the music volume halved, and combat/boss songs (meant to lift) come out quieter than the calm area songs.
fix: 1) In ace_import.py add a 'phone' pre-filter before loudnorm: low-shelf -4 dB at 120 Hz + gentle 2-4 kHz presence +1.5 dB, and measure loudness on a 150 Hz high-passed copy (normalise what the phone actually plays to -16) for the listed songs; reimport (--reimport-all keeps the chosen takes). 2) Cheap runtime alternative: on phones (DisplayMode.is_phone()) put an AudioEffectFilter low-shelf (-5 dB @ 140 Hz) + AudioEffectCompressor on the Music bus; leave desktop flat. Add the per-song phone-loss number to the loudness audit.
audio_needed: Optional: re-render or EQ the 33 listed bass-heavy songs
needs_tom: Listen on the phone after the fix: farm -> town -> hideout -> a combat song should feel level, combat a little louder.

title: Overall output is quiet on a phone and has no safety limiter: music sits at about -26 LUFS at default settings (file -16, MUSIC_DB -8, bus 8/10 = -1.9 dB), SFX jingles ~8 LU above it, and the Master bus has no limiter
repro: Gain chain at defaults: music -16 LUFS file + MUSIC_DB -8 + Settings _db(8) -1.9 = ~-26 LUFS (night duck -30). Even at 10/10 music is -24 LUFS; mobile games usually land at -16..-14 LUFS out of the speaker, so Tom has to max the phone volume. Jingles (left alone by sfx_soften, -12.6..-16 LUFS, peaks -0.5..-1 dBFS) play at -4 dB = about -17..-20, i.e. 6-9 LU over the song. 6 SFX voices + steps + rec voices + music + ambience can sum past 0 dBFS with nothing catching it (default_bus_layout.tres has no effects).
fix: Raise MUSIC_DB to about -4 (keep the ratio to SFX by trimming jingles: add "j_": -3.0 to GROUP_DB, keep j_buy/j_confirm at 0). Add an AudioEffectLimiter (ceiling -1 dB, threshold -3 dB) on Master in default_bus_layout.tres (and in Settings.ensure_buses for safety). Keep it soft so the -16 LUFS songs aren't squashed.
needs_tom: After the change, check the default volume on the phone at a normal media volume.

title: Ambience beds are not levelled to one reference (-18.7..-28.7 LUFS) so the dB tables in Ambience mean different things per bed; town_day ends up ~-45 LUFS (inaudible) while crowd is 7 LU hotter; several beds are 0.4-3 s loops that repeat audibly
repro: ebur128 over audio/amb/*.ogg (non-spot): most beds -25.3..-26.6 LUFS, but crowd -18.7, rain_roof -18.8, arcade_floor -19.2, leaves -20.2, town_day -22.1, lava -22.4, rec_alley -27.8, basement_drips -28.7. With Ambience's dB on top and Ambience bus 7/10: town_day -22.1-20-3.1 = ~-45 LUFS under a -26 LUFS town song (16+ LU under: nothing on a phone), festival crowd -18.7-14 = -36. Loop lengths: machines 0.39 s (smithy/forge/workshop interiors and iron rail areas: a 2.5 Hz buzz), birds_dawn 1.3 s (the farm's dawn chorus repeats every 1.3 s at -7 dB, the loudest bird bed), campfire 1.4 s, boiling 2.4 s, purr_loop 2.8 s, wind_strong 3.0 s (blizzard/colony_ice).
fix: In cc0_import.py normalise every bed to -26 LUFS on import (spots stay peak-levelled) and rm+rewrite the off ones; then retune town_day to about -12 so the town has a day hum. Replace beds shorter than ~8 s with longer takes from the same CC0 packs (or build them by crossfading 3-4 random slices of the source into a 20-30 s loop in cc0_import.py). Add bed length >= 8 s and level -26 +/-1.5 to sfx_audit.py.
audio_needed: Longer loops (20 s+) for machines, birds_dawn, campfire, boiling, purr_loop, wind_strong (CC0 packs already in use, or ACE)

title: Volume steps are uneven: 0-10 maps to linear amplitude, so 1->5 spans 14 dB while 6->10 spans only 4.4 dB (the top half of the control barely changes anything)
repro: Settings._db(v) = linear_to_db(v/10): 1=-20.0, 2=-14.0, 3=-10.5, 4=-8.0, 5=-6.0, 6=-4.4, 7=-3.1, 8=-1.9, 9=-0.9, 10=0 dB. Defaults 8/8/7 sit where three taps of '-' are hard to hear, then 3->1 suddenly drops 10 dB.
fix: Use an even dB scale: _db(v) = -80 if v<=0 else -3.0 * (10 - v) (1 = -27 dB, 5 = -15, 8 = -6, 10 = 0), and re-pick defaults (music 8, sound 8, nature 7 then become -6/-6/-9; raise MUSIC_DB by ~4 dB at the same time so the default music level doesn't drop). Saved values keep working (same 0-10 range). Update tools/systems_test.gd if it asserts a dB value.

title: Sound settings only exist inside a running game (Menu > Options): the title screen, where the loudest unlevelled song (title, -14.2 LUFS) plays first, has no volume or mute control; no 'reset to defaults'; unmute restarts the song from 0
repro: grep title.gd: no Settings/mute/volume rows. A phone player in a quiet room has to start or load a save before they can turn music down. Options has no defaults button. Music.toggle_mute() stop()s both players when muting and play()s from position 0 on unmute (the boss/area song restarts).
fix: Add a small 'Sound' button on the title screen that opens the same three volume rows + mute (factor the rows out of game_menu.gd into a static helper, e.g. Settings.add_audio_rows(parent, refresh)). Add 'Reset sound to defaults' under the rows. In toggle_mute, store _player.get_playback_position() and resume with play(pos) (muting the Master bus is already enough; stopping isn't needed). Consider 'Ambience' instead of 'Nature' in the gangster arc (city hum, neon street).

title: No dip under dialogue: story lines, letters and talk blips sit on top of the full area/combat song
repro: Dialogue never calls Music; blips play at -9.5 dB (-4 + talk_blip -5.5) over the song. During boss intros and story beats (combat_elite/boss songs, -16 LUFS, heavy low end) the blips and portraits feel unattended.
fix: Dialogue._next/_close: Music.set_duck_layer("talk", -3.0, 0.3 s attack, 0.6 s release) while the box is open (uses the layered duck from the battle-duck finding). Keep it small (-3 dB) so the song still carries the scene.

title: Boss-card roar (all 3 takes) and stomp.ogg are almost pure sub-bass: on a phone speaker they lose 9-13 dB, so the boss intro sting is close to silent
repro: Peak level full vs after a 2x 200 Hz high-pass: roar -7.0 -> -18.6 (-11.6 dB), roar_2 -4.7 -> -13.4, roar_3 -6.2 -> -9.5, stomp -5.7 -> -18.3 (-12.6) while stomp_2/_3 lose ~0; hit/boom/shot/cannon lose 0-2 dB. game_map.gd:1748 plays 'roar' on every boss card (with shake), so on the phone the card appears with a faint rumble, and stomp takes are wildly uneven (1 in 3 nearly silent).
fix: In sfx_soften.py add a 'phone presence' pass for files whose >200 Hz energy is >8 dB under full band: gentle saturation/harmonic exciter (ffmpeg 'aexciter' or asoftclip on a band-passed copy mixed in) or a +4 dB shelf at 300-1200 Hz, then re-level; or replace roar/stomp with takes that have a mid-range growl. Add the phone-loss figure to the soften log and flag > 8 dB.
audio_needed: Optionally new roar takes with mid-range body (CC0 or ACE kit)

title: Every song is the same -16 LUFS, so there is no intended level shape: combat/boss songs don't lift over area songs, and wide-range calm songs (house LRA 7.5, chapel 7.4, mega_wind_storm 7.7, title_musicbox 6.7, forest 6.1, mega_gloam 6.6) dip under the ambience beds in their quiet bars
repro: ebur128 integrated: all 88 levelled songs -16.1..-15.7 LUFS regardless of role. DangerMusic climbing farm -> combat_light -> danger -> boss changes style but not level (and after the phone-speaker loss the bass-heavy combat songs end up quieter than the farm). House/chapel quiet passages fall ~5-7 LU under their average, i.e. ~-33 LUFS effective at night duck, level with rain_roof/hearth beds.
fix: Add a per-song trim table in Music (TRACK_DB, applied in _start/_set target volume: MUSIC_DB + TRACK_DB.get(name, 0) + ducks): interiors/night/lullaby -1.5, area 0, combat_light/battle +1, danger/raid/combat_elite +1.5, boss*/mega boss +2 (keep within the new Master limiter). For the high-LRA calm songs add a light compressor pass in ace_import.py (LRA=7 in loudnorm instead of 11) on reimport.
needs_tom: Taste call: should fights get louder than exploring? (proposal: about +1.5 dB)

title: Every song change restarts the new song from 0:00, so each skirmish (DangerMusic: area -> combat after 0.25-0.6 s, back after 5 s grace) replays the area song's intro; mute/unmute also restarts
repro: Music._start() always calls _player.play() with no position. Farm with a few slimes: combat_light cuts in, foe dies, 5 s later farm.ogg fades back in from its first bar; next slime, same again - the player hears the first 10-20 s of the farm song over and over. Same for town <-> shop interiors (house/shop songs restart every door).
fix: Keep a small resume map in Music: on fade-out store {track: [playback_position, Time.get_ticks_msec()]}; in _start, if the track was left less than ~90 s ago and isn't in ONCE, play(pos) (wrap with stream length). Combat/boss songs still start from 0 (their intros are the cue).

title: UI clicks get random pitch: short ui_/menu_/j_confirm-length sounds fall under the 0.93-1.07 pitch drift meant for swings and steps
repro: Music.sfx(): pitch is randomised for every stream <= 0.45 s unless the name starts with j_ or is in a short list; ui_tap, ui_back, menu_open, page, equip, keypress are all short, so menu taps wobble +/-7% (a semitone), which reads as sloppy in menus and on the volume +/- buttons.
fix: Exempt names starting with ui_, menu_, page, equip, keypress, talk_blip (blip already sets its own pitch) from the drift, e.g. a NO_DRIFT prefix list next to GROUP_DB.

title: Random takes of the same sound differ by 6-18 dB, so Music.sfx's random pick makes common actions jump in volume (rock_break, cash, shot, shot_shotgun, harvest, chest_open, servo, freeze...)
repro: Loudest-100 ms RMS per take (mono, 22 kHz): servo -34.5 vs servo_2 -16.7 (17.8 dB); freeze -16.2 / _2 -26.9; rock_break -15.4 / -22.6 / -25.2; cash -19.2 / -16.8 / -25.6 (gangster coin pickups); shot_shotgun -14.2 / -22.9; shot -23.1 / -15.6 / -18.9; shot_heavy -20.9 / -14.2 / -17.2; drop -15.8 / -19.2 / -23.3; chest_open -18.0 / -25.8; harvest -17.3 / -18.8 / -23.6; cash_register -18.8/-17.8/-24.1; fireworks, spell_ice, pin_tap, pin_crash 6-8 dB. sfx_soften only moves each file 75% toward its target (to keep booms bigger than clicks), which is right across names but leaves takes of one name unequal.
fix: In sfx_soften.py, after the per-file pass, level each take group (name, name_2, name_3) to the group's median loudest-100ms RMS (within +/-1.5 dB), --force for the listed groups (rm+write: hardlinks). Add a take-spread check (> 3 dB fails) to sfx_audit.py.

title: Music at 0/10 (or All sound off) still downloads songs on the web build: _fetch and the ~23 MB prefetch queue ignore the volume/mute settings
repro: Set Music volume 0 (bus muted) or All sound off, play the web build on a phone: Music.play() still calls _fetch(track) for every area change and _prefetch_next() quietly pulls PREFETCH + PREFETCH_<arc> (16 songs, about 23 MB of the 121 MB streamed set) over mobile data, for music the player can't hear.
fix: Skip _fetch/_prefetch_next while int(Settings.get_v("music_vol")) <= 0 or _muted (play() just remembers _current); when the volume goes above 0 / unmute, call play(_current) again (Settings.apply_audio or toggle_mute can poke Music) so the wanted song is fetched then.

title: The night/storm music duck (-4 / -5 dB, meant to let crickets and rain through) also applies to combat and boss songs, so night fights are quieter than day fights
repro: Ambience._evaluate sets duck -4 outdoors at night and -3..-5 in storms with no check of what is playing; DangerMusic doesn't touch the duck. A night slime pack or a storm boss plays its combat song 4-5 dB under the same song by day.
fix: In Ambience._evaluate, use 0 duck while DangerMusic has a tier >= 1 (expose DangerMusic.tier() or Music.now_playing() in DangerMusic.TRACKS/boss tracks); with the layered duck from the battle-duck finding this is just env layer = 0 during danger.

title: Jingles are peak-normalised, not loudness-matched: 6 LU spread between stingers (j_page/j_region/j_treasure -13.8..-14.0 LUFS vs craft_done -19.7, quest_done -19.4, levelup -18.8, j_battle_won -18.5)
repro: ace_kits.fade() scales every cut jingle to 0.89 peak (-1 dBFS); sfx_soften skips j_*. ebur128: j_page -13.8, j_region -13.9, j_treasure -14.0, j_secret -15.0, j_campaign_won -15.3, j_victory -15.6, j_heart -15.7, j_morning -16.1, j_gift/j_battle_start -16.7, j_skill/j_birthday -17.3, j_battle_won -18.5, levelup -18.8, quest_done -19.4, craft_done -19.7. Reading a journal page (j_page) blares ~5 LU over finishing a quest (quest_done), the reward that should feel biggest.
fix: In ace_kits.py replace the peak scale with loudness matching (measure integrated/short-term loudness, target -16 LUFS, cap peaks at -1.5 dBFS); for quest_done/levelup/craft_done (not ACE cuts) do the same in sfx_soften with a 'jingle' target. Then GROUP_DB can carry the intent: j_battle_won/j_campaign_won/quest_done/levelup 0, j_page/j_secret -2, j_buy/j_confirm -3.

title: Audio keeps playing when the game is backgrounded: nothing fades or mutes the Master bus on focus-out (only a save happens)
repro: grep FOCUS_OUT: game_map.gd saves, touch_controls/arcade pause, Music/Ambience do nothing. Web build: switch to another tab on desktop, or (browser-dependent) to another app on Android Chrome - the area song, ambience beds and spot sounds carry on under whatever the player switched to. Desktop windowed build keeps playing while unfocused too.
fix: Music._notification: on NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_FOCUS_OUT / WM_WINDOW_FOCUS_OUT / APPLICATION_PAUSED tween the Master bus to -80 dB over 0.3 s (separate from the user's mute flag) and restore on FOCUS_IN / RESUMED. Add a setting 'Sound in background: off/on' (default off) next to All sound.
needs_tom: Check on the phone: does the song keep going after switching apps?

title: Proposed target mix for the fix package (numbers for a fix agent to tune Music/Settings/Ambience constants against)
repro: Today at defaults (measured): music ~-26 LUFS (night -30), ambience beds -33..-45, SFX actions loudest-100ms ~-20 dBFS, UI clicks ~-29, steps ~-38, jingles -17..-24 with no duck. Music is the quietest layer apart from steps, and the phone speaker removes another 5-10 dB from bass-heavy songs.
fix: Targets at default settings, phone speaker: music -21 LUFS (area), -19.5 combat, -19 boss; night duck -3; ambience beds -30 (storm -26); actions -18; UI clicks -24 (no pitch drift); talk blip -26 with -3 dB music dip; jingles -17 with music ducked -10 dB (0.12 s attack, 0.8 s release); steps -32. Implementation: even-dB Settings curve (-3 dB per step), defaults music 9 / sound 8 / ambience 7, MUSIC_DB -2, TRACK_DB per role, layered duck (env/talk/jingle), Master limiter -1 dB ceiling, optional phone low-shelf on the Music bus. Verify with a probe that renders 30 s of farm + combat + gift into a wav via AudioEffectRecord on Master and measures LUFS/peaks (add as tools/mix_probe.gd).
needs_tom: Phone listening pass after the package: the default should be comfortable at about half phone volume.

title: Gangster cash pickup is ~6 dB louder than the penguin coin and gets pitch drift: Music.sfx swaps coin->cash_pickup before the GROUP_DB and no-drift lookups, so neither the coin -3 dB group nor the coin pitch exemption applies
repro: Music.sfx(): name = Money.sfx_name(name) runs first, then _group_db(name) and the pitch rule (name in [..., 'coin', ...]) see 'cash_pickup'. Loudest-100ms: coin -24.1/-20.9/-20.9 vs cash_pickup -17.8/-18.4/-23.7, plus the missing -3 dB group trim -> every sale and pickup in the gangster arc is ~5-6 dB hotter than in the penguin arc, and its pitch wobbles +/-7%.
fix: Add "cash_pickup": -3.0 (or -5 to match the hotter files) to GROUP_DB and 'cash_pickup' to the no-drift list; or compute group/pitch from the pre-swap name. Also level the cash_pickup takes with sfx_soften's 'coin' target (-18) by adding ('cash_pickup', -18.0) to TARGETS.

title: UI-type sounds missing from GROUP_DB play as loud as hits and level-ups: scroll_tick (15 calls, repeats while scrolling), tab (menu tabs) and nope (30 calls, every refused action) land at ~-19 dB while ui_tap sits at ~-27
repro: Loudest-100ms after -4 dB voice level + GROUP_DB: ui_tap -26.8, pickup -26.4, dry_click -27.9 vs scroll_tick -18.9, tab -18.9, nope -18.9 - same as hit -18.7, levelup -18.5, quest_done -18.6. Scrolling a list or flicking tabs ticks at combat-hit level, and the refusal buzz (wrong tool, full bag, locked door) is as loud as finishing a quest.
fix: GROUP_DB: "scroll_tick": -8.0, "tab": -6.0, "nope": -4.0 (and add them to sfx_soften TARGETS at -20 so the files match the ui_ group); exempt scroll_tick/tab from pitch drift with the other UI names.
